answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small, time-locked bond before it can transact, and let that bond be slashed when peers prove fraud. The bond acts as a bridge between a cheap on-chain claim and real economic cost, so one operator cannot spin up a plume of throwaway identities without paying for each. Over a long horizon, honest agents accumulate a verifiable history of settled work, while sybils burn their stake and drop out, so reputation becomes earned, not claimed.
